findings.title: Local disconnect and provider revocation are different outcomes
findings.expectedBehavior: Credentials are removed locally, while unconfirmed remote revocation remains visible after reload/reconnect.
findings.changes: Persists sanitized revocation_unknown before removing local access and records provider result afterward. Durable rows and backwards-compatible local record arrays preserve older unresolved revocations when a new grant refresh succeeds.
evidence: token-recovery.test.ts: failed revoke clears credentials, unresolved metadata survives reload, later successful refresh cannot hide older uncertainty
remainingVerification: Manual provider account-settings review remains required when remote revocation is unconfirmed; the app does not claim that access was revoked.

findings.title: Revocation needs provider-specific response contracts
findings.expectedBehavior: Each provider response is interpreted by its documented success contract, with unknown results disclosed.
findings.changes: Google/form and Notion require HTTP 200; GitHub requires 204; Slack requires HTTP success plus ok=true and revoked=true. Arbitrary 2xx outcomes do not become confirmed revocation.
evidence: token-recovery.test.ts: provider contract table covers success and unsupported response codes/body fields
remainingVerification: Official contracts reviewed: developers.google.com OAuth web-server; developers.notion.com/reference/revoke-token; docs.github.com OAuth app token deletion; docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/auth.revoke. No real revocation performed.
